answer: An agent marketplace requires every seller to lock a $100 bond for 30 days, with payment released only after a verifiable compute task passes its checks; a provably false result forfeits the bond. This creates an oasis of accountable trade: an attacker building an island of 1,000 fake sellers must immobilize $100,000 and risks losing it on fraudulent jobs. New aliases may arrive like a zephyr, but each carries the same capital requirement.
